evidence:
Checked the arXiv HTML at https://arxiv.org/html/2311.07568 (v2) and the arXiv LaTeX source.

Claim 1: "minimum margin is at most any averaged class-weighted margin".
- Morwani Sec. 3 is "Theoretical Approach", with 3.1 Binary, 3.2 Multi-Class and 3.3 Blueprint.
- Sec. 3.2 defines the class-weighted margin g'(θ,x,y) = f[y] - Σ_{y'≠y} τ(x,y)[y'] f[y'], where τ is any distribution over the incorrect labels.
- It states verbatim: "Note that g′(θ,x,y) ≥ g(θ,x,y) as g′ replaces the max by a weighted sum."
- Sec. 3 also writes γ* = max_θ min_{q∈P(D)} E_q[g].
- So min_D g ≤ E_q[g] ≤ E_q[g'] for any q and τ. This supports the sentence, and the direction is correct.
- Our uniform q with a point-mass τ on y−δ is an admissible τ.

Claim 2: the η_{u,v,w} quantity.
- η_{u,v,w}(δ) := E_{a,b}[(u(a)+v(b))^2 w(a+b−δ)] is defined in Appendix F ("Proofs for cyclic groups", the proof of Thm 7). It does not appear in the main text.
- It is a single quadratic neuron's mean logit at the candidate δ below the label.
- Our η_θ(δ) = E_x[f(θ,x)[y(x)−δ]] is the sum over neurons of this quantity, extended to n operands, so calling it a "network-level analogue" is accurate and the notation is exact.

The bib entry (title, authors, ICLR 2024, arXiv:2311.07568) is correct. Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c8-morwani-sec3-avg/CHECK.md.
